scope: Read-only verification executed to support a retraining runbook for the decision model. Every entry below is either (a) measured/observed by a command recorded here, or (b) explicitly labelled as an estimate. No training run was performed, no optimizer step was taken, no checkpoint or corpus was written, and no network call was made.
explicit_non_claims: No model was trained, fine-tuned, distilled or otherwise modified.
No checkpoint file was created, overwritten or touched; the production checkpoint directory was only read.
No corpus was materialized; both corpus builders were invoked in self-test/no-write modes only.
No accuracy, abstention, calibration, token-saving or readiness claim is made about any retrained model, because none exists.
The wall-clock figures under wall_clock_projection are arithmetic projections from measured components, not an observed full run.
The LoRA/BF16 recipe in docs/GATE_CONTRASTIVE_PROTOCOL_V1.md section 7 was NOT executed and was NOT verified as runnable on this machine; the probe shows it is refused.
No network access was used (web tools were not called; corpus builders and trainer entry points ran with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 / local-only checkpoint loading).

The probe measured a lower bound on memory (no optimizer.step()); the real peak is estimated at ~8.9 GiB.
Timings are specific to this M5-class Mac and this torch build; they are not a cross-machine benchmark.
The engineering corpus does not exist yet and its builder currently fails its own self-test, so no measurement on the actual domain-adaptation data was possible.
Whether the 0.6B backbone can express the required engineering discrimination at all is untested; docs/GATE_CONTRASTIVE_PROTOCOL_V1.md section 10.6 names this as a live failure mode.
The engineering contrastive labels are programmatic and not human-reviewed; the acceptance endpoints therefore measure agreement with a synthetic oracle, not with human engineering judgement.
